market_outlook: This is a company-specific earnings note covering Tuesday September 22 before-market-open reporters. No broad directional market view is expressed by Adam in this edition.

company_items.summary: AutoZone beat FQ4 EPS by roughly two dollars ($56.05 vs. $54.03 estimate), but quality was poor — the upside was driven by tariff refunds adding 145 basis points to gross margins and a non-cash LIFO benefit adding 105 basis points. Domestic comps missed badly at +1.6% versus the +3.1% expected, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final eight weeks and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced an acquisition of RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional ~$106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80–90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex in the fast-growing physical AI and robotics perception space.

MillerKnoll delivered solid FQ1 EPS upside at 53 cents versus the 36-cent estimate, and importantly the beat holds even excluding an 11-cent tariff refund tailwind — core EPS of 42 cents still topped consensus. Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million versus the $943.2 million expected, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed slightly but EPS guidance was left unchanged, and FQ2 EPS guidance midpoint is in line with consensus.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November 1, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on through the transition. Hau brings prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. This is a leadership transition event with no financial results attached.

THOR missed FQ4 EPS at 78 cents versus the 87-cent estimate as gross margins collapsed 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4%, far below the 13.85% expected, with management citing stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation squeezing household budgets. Revenue of $2.311 billion was slightly above the $2.17 billion estimate but still down 8.4% year-over-year. Some bright spots emerged: dealer inventory is healthy, structural cost actions are underway, and the North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75% year-over-year, though the company declined to provide formal fiscal 2027 guidance.

Viking shares spiked in pre-market trading after reporting positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in participants. The result is a meaningful positive data point in the competitive GLP-1 obesity drug landscape. This reinforces Viking as a credible challenger in the weight-loss drug market.

sectors: RV/recreational vehicle sector faces headwinds per THOR commentary — stubborn interest rates, fuel costs, and inflation are keeping retail soft. GLP-1/obesity drug sector gets a fresh positive data point from Viking's VK2735 trial. Robotics and physical AI perception is in focus with Cognex's RealSense acquisition.
tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific note covering the before-the-open reporters for Tuesday September 22nd. No broad macro or Fed commentary in this edition — let's go straight to the names.

Starting with AutoZone. The auto parts retailer beat on fiscal fourth quarter earnings per share — fifty-six dollars and five cents versus the fifty-four dollar and three cent estimate. But do not mistake the headline for quality. The beat was entirely manufactured by tariff refunds, which added 145 basis points to gross margins, and a non-cash LIFO accounting benefit worth another 105 basis points. Strip those out and the picture looks worse. Domestic comparable store sales came in at plus 1.6 percent — the Street was expecting plus 3.1 percent. And operating expenses as a percent of sales rose 100 basis points year over year. Management tried to put a positive spin on it, noting that sales improved meaningfully in the final eight weeks of the quarter versus the first eight weeks, and they said they feel well positioned for fiscal 2027 sales growth. Mixed read overall — the beat is low quality but the forward commentary is constructive.

Next, Cognex is acquiring RealSense — the market leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception and physical AI — for roughly 500 million dollars upfront plus another 106 and a half million. RealSense is expected to do 80 to 90 million in revenue, growing more than 50 percent year over year. This is a bullish strategic move, planting Cognex squarely in the physical AI and robotics perception space at a time when that market is accelerating fast.

MillerKnoll delivered a clean beat on fiscal first quarter earnings — 53 cents versus 36 cents expected. And critically, even backing out the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, they still beat at 42 cents. Revenue missed at 923 million versus 943 million expected, down 3.3 percent organically. But orders grew 3.5 percent year over year. Fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed slightly while EPS guidance held. Net bullish read here.

THOR Industries missed fiscal fourth quarter earnings at 78 cents versus 87 cents expected. Gross margins fell 230 basis points year over year to 12.4 percent — well below the nearly 14 percent the Street was modeling. Management's tone was cautious, pointing to stubborn interest rates, fuel costs, and inflation keeping consumers on the sidelines. No formal fiscal 2027 guidance was provided. Some positives — dealer inventory is clean, structural cost cuts are underway, and North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75 percent year over year. But the headline miss and cautious tone make this a bearish read.

Finally, Viking Therapeutics is spiking in pre-market after reporting positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735 — showing 22 percent weight loss. That is a headline number that gets attention in this space, and the stock is responding accordingly. Clearly bullish.

Bottom line for the session — no broad market call in this note, but the key single-stock reads are: Viking to the upside on strong GLP-1 data, MillerKnoll quietly solid, Cognex making a bold physical AI bet, AutoZone a quality question, and THOR a clear miss in a tough consumer environment. Stay focused on the individual setups today.
